title: Square Feet and Square Meters in Real Estate
h1: Square feet and square metres — the real-estate conversion nobody double-checks
description: Apartments listed at 800 sq ft rarely convert to a round metric number. Here is the exact factor, and the local measurement conventions that shift the number by 10%.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against NIST SP 811 §B.8 and RICS Property Measurement

hero: The math is one factor. The trap is what each country counts as 'floor area' — balconies, walls, shafts and all.
body: 1 sq ft = 0.09290304 m² exactly. That is the easy part. The hard part is that a 100 m² Parisian apartment measured under the Loi Carrez and a 100 m² Tokyo apartment measured under the Japanese senyuu-menseki refer to different physical spaces. The unit is the same; the definition of what to measure is not.

The US typically quotes gross living area — inside faces of exterior walls, including interior walls but excluding garages. France's Loi Carrez excludes any space with less than 1.8 m ceiling height. Japan's senyuu-menseki excludes balconies and shared corridors entirely. The UK's RICS IPMS 3 sits between the two.
## Worked example — a 90 m² London flat

A 90 m² flat under RICS IPMS 3 converts to 969 sq ft. If the same physical space were remeasured under the US 'gross living area' convention including a 6 m² balcony, it becomes 96 m² = 1,033 sq ft. A 7% listing difference from the same walls — before anyone rounds.

Any listing showing 800 sq ft = 74 m² is doing honest maths. Any listing showing 800 sq ft = 80 m² is either rounding or reporting two different measurements. Multiply sq ft by 0.0929 as a spot-check.
Multiply sq ft by 0.0929 for m². Multiply m² by 10.76 for sq ft. And always ask which measurement standard the number was captured under.

faqs.a: A Japanese area unit equal to about 3.306 m² (~35.6 sq ft). Still used for property price comparisons in Japan.

faqs.q: Do balconies count in floor area?
faqs.a: Depends entirely on jurisdiction. US: sometimes. France: no if ceiling under 1.8 m. Japan: never.

faqs.q: How big is 1 acre in square metres?
faqs.a: 4,046.86 m² — or roughly a 63.6 m × 63.6 m square.
